specification.problem: Discrete-time Grover-coined flip-flop quantum walk on the plain 4-cycle C4, built as a unitary U = S C on a 2-qubit position register and a 2-qubit coin register. The goal is to check whether the antipodal node 2 is reached with probability 1 from the arc state at node 0. This is the smallest building block of the abstract's study of antipodal perfect state transfer (PST) on modified C4/C6/C8 graphs.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Only the plain unmodified C4 with the Grover coin G_2 and the flip-flop shift, with initial arc state |0,0> and t = 1..4. The abstract's modified graphs (chords, extra nodes) are not specified in the abstract and are not constructed. Also outside scope: C6, C8, the other coin choices, the three generalised graph families, continuous-time walks, initial-state robustness, interpolation, and decoherence. The circuit yields only the unitary; evaluating P_t is external analysis. No black-box query claims are made.

symbols.meaning: coin/arc label at a node; c=0 is the arc to v+1 mod 4, c=1 is the arc to v-1 mod 4; c=2,3 are unused padding
one-step walk unitary U = S C
Grover coin applied at each node on the used arc subspace
symbols.domain: unitary, identity on padding coin states

symbols.meaning: probability of being at the antipodal node 2 after t steps
node degree; d=2 on plain C4

equations.label: Initial arc state
equations.description: Arc at node 0 pointing to neighbour 1, prepared from |0000> with no gates since the binary encoding of 0,0 is all zeros.
equations.justification: Chosen as the tiny instance; the abstract does not give the initial state. The sketch's X gates are unnecessary under this labelling.
assumptions: Basis ordering |v,c> with position qubits first, integer encoding of v and c in binary

equations.label: Grover coin
equations.latex: G_d=2|s_d\rangle\langle s_d|-I_d,\quad |s_d\rangle=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt d}\sum_{c<d}|c\rangle,\quad G_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad C=\sum_v |v\rangle\langle v|\otimes (G_2\oplus I_2)
equations.description: Grover coin on each node's d-dimensional arc space; for C4, d=2 so it is X on c in {0,1}, with padding states c=2,3 left unchanged.
equations.justification: Standard Grover coin. The abstract mentions three coin choices but does not name them; Grover is taken from the method plan.
assumptions: Grover coin is one of the paper's three coins (unverified)

equations.label: Flip-flop shift on C4
equations.description: Flip-flop shift mapping arc (v,w) to the reversed arc (w,v), expressed in the label convention.
equations.justification: Derived from the stated label convention (c=0 to v+1, c=1 to v-1); the reverse of the arc v to v+1 is the arc v+1 to v, which has label 1 there.
assumptions: Padding states fixed by identity so S is a permutation of all 16 states

equations.label: Step and evolution
equations.description: On C4 the Grover flip-flop walk reduces to ballistic motion with a fixed coin label, so U^4 = I on the used subspace. From |0,0>, U^2|0,0>=|2,0>.
equations.justification: Direct computation from eq_2 and eq_3: C maps c=0 to c=1, then S moves v to v-1 with label 0.

equations.label: Antipodal probability
equations.description: Probability at the antipodal node 2; PST is declared when P_t equals 1 exactly. For plain C4 from |0,0>, P_2=1.
equations.abstract_quote: perfect state transfer between antipodal nodes of discrete time quantum walks
equations.justification: The abstract studies antipodal PST; the probability form is the standard way to test it. The strict form (transfer to a specific arc state) is a stricter variant that is not used here.
assumptions: PST defined as unit probability at node 2 for some t

registers.name: pos
registers.role: node index v in {0,1,2,3}, binary integer encoding, qubits 0-1

registers.name: coin
registers.role: arc label c in {0..3}, binary integer encoding, qubits 2-3; only c=0,1 used on C4

specification.initial_state: |v=0>|c=0> = |0000>, the arc from node 0 toward node 1.

steps.description: Prepare |0,0>, which is the all-zero state (no gates).

Build U = S C as an explicit 16x16 unitary from classical adjacency data: first the block-diagonal Grover coin (X on the coin LSB acting only on c in {0,1}, identity for c=2,3), then the flip-flop permutation. Compile the permutation and coin into standard gates, and repeat U for t steps (t=1..4).
External analysis: compute P_t from the simulated statevector and check P_t=1 (expected at t=2 for plain C4).

specification.measurement: No measurement in the circuit. The simulated final state is analysed externally for the probability on node 2, i.e. the position register equals 10 (binary).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compute P_t = sum over coin values of |amplitude at (v=2,c)|^2 for each t and flag PST when P_t = 1 within numerical tolerance.
assumptions: Chosen smallest instance: plain C4, Grover coin, flip-flop shift, initial arc state |0,0>.
Modified graphs (chords, extra nodes) are not constructed because the abstract does not specify them.
The coin used is assumed to match one of the paper's three coins; this is unverified.
The walk on plain C4 is trivially ballistic, so this instance demonstrates PST mechanics but not the paper's nontrivial modified-graph results.
